facts.fact: Parukutty's daughter is named Minnu (six) and her son Chandu (nine).
facts.why: needed because Neela habitually learns names and uses Minnu's cough as the pretext for trading for a coin.

facts.fact: Rema pays Parukutty's early death-gift as twelve new silver coins, more than the salt-factor debt plus tally fee; Rema writes the receipt herself because Ittan's clerk is held.
facts.why: needed because the beat requires the early crown-silver payment.

facts.fact: The widow's coin and the scouts' coins share a die flaw: the lowest leaf of the pepper sprig is doubled, and they weigh the same to a grain on the granary pepper scale. Neela trades a worn panam for one bright coin.
facts.why: needed because clue C14 (same mint run for widows and raiders) must be memorable and weighable; Devan holds the satchel evidence from ch 14.

facts.fact: The black book is kept on a dry ledge cut into the Resin House well shaft a few man-lengths down, above the water. Neela and Ammu dropped a pebble down it at eleven and noticed the wrong sound.
facts.why: needed because the beat requires Devan to climb the well shaft while Neela, in shape, cannot.

facts.fact: Plan: Neela goes over the east wall as the leopard, quiets the hounds, opens the drain, and lifts the well-house bar; Devan comes over at the ridge party's signal, goes down the shaft on a rope, and holds the book from then until Neela turns back at dawn. Devan's rule: if he begins reading a page for any reason, she must stop him.
facts.why: needed to set up the mutual veto in chapter 12.

facts.fact: They ride from Kettamala at first light on the raid day and reach the ridge above the Resin House by dusk; the last night in the warden's chamber is the night before the raid.
facts.why: needed to fix when Neela skips resin.
